diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Large component is hard to read and change
diagnostics.message: Component "ReminderOffsetTogglePanel" is over 300 lines long, which is hard to read & change. Split it into a few smaller components.
diagnostics.help: Pull each section into its own component so the parent is easier to read, test, and change.

diagnostics.title: await inside a loop
diagnostics.message: This makes the for…of loop slow because each await runs one after another, so collect the independent calls & run them together with `await Promise.all(items.map(...))`
diagnostics.help: Collect the items, then use `await Promise.all(items.map(...))` so independent work runs at the same time

diagnostics.title: React function has high control-flow complexity
diagnostics.message: `LoginPage` has cyclomatic complexity 34, cognitive complexity 42, and maximum nesting depth 4, so its React logic is hard to understand and change. Extract independent branches into components or hooks.
diagnostics.help: Extract independent render branches and state logic into focused components or hooks until the control flow is easy to follow.

diagnostics.title: Many related useState calls
diagnostics.message: "LoginPage" updates 5 separate useState values in one place — state that changes together is easier to keep consistent as a single useReducer action.
diagnostics.help: Group state that always changes together into `useReducer` so one dispatched action describes the whole transition instead of a list of setter calls.

diagnostics.title: State only used in handlers
diagnostics.message: Each update to "challengeId" redraws your component for nothing because this useState is set but never shown on screen.
diagnostics.help: Use useRef instead of useState when the value is only set and never shown on screen. `ref.current = ...` updates it without redrawing the component.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.message: This is slow because new Intl.NumberFormat() rebuilds on every call inside a function, so move it to the top of the file, or wrap it in useMemo
diagnostics.help: Move `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)` to the top of the file or wrap it in `useMemo`. Building one is slow, so don't redo it on every call
